questions.q_en: The homophone for the word 'build' is:
questions.solution_en:
Homophones are words that sound the same but have different meanings and spellings.

"Build" and "billed" are pronounced the same, but they have different meanings:

Build - To construct something.

Billed - Past tense of "bill," meaning to send or receive an invoice.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

Built - The past tense and past participle of "build." It means something has been constructed or made.

Bile - A digestive fluid produced by the liver, or metaphorically, it can mean anger or bitterness.

Belt - A strip of material used to hold up clothing or as a mechanical device to transmit motion. It can also mean to hit something forcefully (e.g., "belted the ball").

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

It has been demanded by the communities to appoint one of their own.
options_en: The communities had demanded it to appoint one of their own.
The communities have demanded it to appoint one of their own.
The communities were demanded it to appoint one of their own.
The communities demanded it to appoint one of their own.
questions.solution_en:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb ['been' here] and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Present Perfect tense. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Present Perfect.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object.

For example:

A new horse has been bought by Arya. (Passive Voice)

Arya has bought a new horse. (Active Voice)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The communities have demanded it to appoint one of their own.

questions.q_en: In the question given below, four statements are given which may or may not contain an error. Choose the one that is grammatically and meaningfully correct.
options_en: The captain steered the ship across the sea.
I want to sea the beautiful views of the coast.
Turn the light on so I can sea.
I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw a see.
questions.solution_en:
Among the given sentences, only sentence a) is error free.

Sentence b): The verb "see" should be used after the infinitive marker "to", instead of the noun "sea".

Sentence c): The modal verb "can" should be followed by the base verb "see", instead of the noun "sea".

Sentence d): The indefinite article "a" is always followed by the noun. So, the verb "see" should be replaced by the noun "sea".

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been split into three segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. If the sentence is free of any errors, mark 'No error' as your answer.

This is the same painting which adorned/ the walls of our ancestral home, / evoking nostalgic memories of bygone eras.
options_en: this is the same painting which adorned
the walls of our ancestral home
evoking nostalgic memories of bygone eras
questions.solution_en:
All, any, the only, the same, none, much, the little, the few, something, anything, nothing and superlative degrees are all followed by 'that' only. They cannot be followed by 'who' or 'which'. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The corrected sentence: This is the same painting that adorned the walls of our ancestral home, evoking nostalgic memories of bygone eras.

Note: · The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

B. By systematically decluttering their physical space and daily schedules, adherents often find that they also declutter their minds, leading to reduced stress and enhanced mental clarity.

Sentence C, starting with "consequently," acts as a conclusion by summarizing the outcome of "this deliberate approach" - the freeing up of resources for more meaningful pursuits.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

Delilah watched smiling as this year's batch of fresh students entered into her classroom. Once all six children were in the room, the door closed with a small snap. Catherine and Isabella, names Delilah knew from the files she had studied carefully in the weeks before the start of the semester, looked around suspiciously but quickly decided that the noise posed no threat. After all they didn't know that the door had closed of its own accord. Delilah gestured towards the six cushioned chairs each behind a sizeable desk and the children took their seats, some more reluctantly than others. Catherine immediately slouched in her chair and crossed her arms in defiance. Ian rested his head lazily in one hand with elbows on the desk. The rest were still nervous about making a bad impression and sat upright, perfectly still. It was a difficult day for the children.

Each child had been tracked and contacted as soon as they turned fourteen. Some were easy to find. Only Catherine had proven difficult but the recruitment department had found her anyway and brought her here, as planned, in time for school. The Owl Academy was a unique, elite school for a very select group of students but Delilah doubted that anyone had heard of it before. Ian's father was very rich and was possibly one of the many wealthy individuals who had heard of the school and tried to buy their child a place. No one knew what the school taught exactly or what its methods were, the only thing that those in the know were certain of was that every child who had ever gone there had grown to be highly successful in whatever field they chose. But no one could buy their way into Owl Academy. There was no application process, no entrance exams, and no open days. Through a process known only to higher administration, students were selected from across the country and invited to attend. Few refused from time to time. Very few invitations were sent each year. This year, all six invitations had been accepted.

Identify whether the given statements are true or false.

A. Owl Academy was similar to any other school in the country.

B. The selection procedure at the Owl Academy was transparent.
options_en: Neither A nor B is true.
Both A and B are true.
A is true and B is false.
A is false and B is true.
questions.solution_en:
The second paragraph of the passage states that "The Owl Academy was a unique, elite school for a very select group of students..." So, the Owl Academy was unlike any other school in the country. Therefore, statement A is false.

The second paragraph also mentions that "There was no application process, no entrance exams, and no open days. Through a process known only to higher administration, students were selected from across the country and invited to attend". questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Dormant
questions.solution_en:
"Dormant" means temporarily inactive or in a state of suspension, like a deep sleep.

a) Sleeping - means being in a state of sleep. This is a synonym for "dormant".

b) Active - means engaging in action or operation; moving or working. This is the direct opposite of being inactive, making "active" the correct antonym.

c) Lazy - means unwilling to work or use energy. While a lazy person might be dormant, this describes a character trait, not a state of being, and is not an opposite.

d) Hidden - means kept out of sight. Something dormant might be hidden, but this word does not relate to its state of activity.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.
